description:
crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:210-223 implements `SetError::new`:

    pub fn new(error_type: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            error_type: error_type.into(),
            ...
        }
    }

There is no check that `error_type` is non-empty. `SetError::new(\"\")`
succeeds and produces a wire form `{\"type\": \"\"}` which is not a valid
RFC 8620 §5.3 SetError. An empty `type` field is meaningless: the
RFC's machine-readable error type identifies which subsequent fields
the client should expect; the empty string identifies nothing.

What a caller depending on this API in production accepts:

1. The constructor's `# Errors` contract is: \"none, regardless of
   input\". A server author that hands user input through to
   `SetError::new` will emit a malformed wire error on empty input.
   Clients deserialize it as `SetError { error_type: \"\".to_owned(), ...
   }` and have to write `if err.error_type.is_empty() { /* server bug */
   }` boilerplate.
2. The doc-comment (methods.rs:201-209) describes the constructor as
   producing \"a wire-shaped error\". It does not warn about the empty
   case. The minimal-serialization test (methods.rs:639) actually
   exercises `SetError::new(\"forbidden\")`, not `SetError::new(\"\")`.

Fix candidates:
- Tighten `SetError::new` to `pub fn new(error_type: impl Into<String>)
  -> Result<Self, ValidationError>` and reject empty input. This is a
  breaking change to the constructor's return type; better done before
  0.2.
- Or: keep `new` permissive, add `new_validated(error_type) -> Result`,
  document `new` as \"trusted input only\".
- Or: do nothing, document the gotcha. Weakest option.

Comparable holes exist on `Id::from(\"\")` and `UTCDate::from(\"\")`,
but those are explicitly gotcha-documented in the README. The
`SetError::new` case is NOT gotcha-documented.
title: SetError::new("") accepts empty error_type despite RFC 8620 5.3 requiring a non-empty type string
